identity_evidence.quote: We report a female neonate presenting at birth

attribution_limitations: The CSF cell count on lumbar puncture is 105 × 10^(6)/L in the main text on day 9, while Supplementary Table S2 lists 23 cells on D9 and 105 cells on D12.
Canakinumab dosing is given as 2 mg/kg every 8 weeks (increased to 3 mg/kg every 8 weeks) in the text, but as mg/(kg·day) and mg/kg/day in the Figure 4 caption.
Growth after canakinumab is described as persistently delayed below the 10th percentile and also as catch-up growth.
All monitored parameters are said to have remained normal throughout follow-up, but a transient CRP rise to 10 mg/L is reported before the second dose.

The sepsis, TORCH, neonatal lupus and HLH differential is described in the discussion; bacterial infection was argued strongly against and HLH criteria were absent, without those two being literally called excluded.
Hearing is described both as normalized completely and as significantly improved.
The text says extensive microbiological investigations returned negative, while Supplementary Table S2 lists CSF NGS organisms (S. epidermidis/C. parapsilosis) on D12.

PRISMA 2020 flow diagram. Adapted from: Page et al. (30).

Urticarial-like rash observed at birth: scattered erythematous plaques of variable size, some coalescing into larger patches. Rash was blanchable on pressure and persisted despite empirical treatment. (The arrow points to the rash).

Figure 3
Genetic findings in the proband and parents: Sanger sequencing confirmed a heterozygous missense mutation in the NLRP3 gene (c.2263G>A, p.Gly755Arg) in the proband. Both parents carried the wild-type all ele, confirming the mutation as de novo.

Figure 4
Longitudinal changes in white blood cell count and C-reactive protein following canakinumab treatment in a case of neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease. The red arrow indicates the time of definitive diagnosis and initiation of canakinumab treatment. The black annotation denotes the canakinumab dosage of 2 mg/(kg·day). During follow-up, a mild elevation in both white blood cell (WBC) count and C-reactive protein (CRP) was observed. After the dosage was adjusted to 3 mg/kg/day, both WBC and CRP decreased to within the normal range.

Figure 5
Diagnostic and management pathway for neonates with persistent Urticaria and systemic inflammation.
